Welcome to Badgemore primary school
The Village School in the Heart of Town.
At Badgemore, we celebrate our differences and embrace our challenges, taking pride and pleasure from success but always striving to be better, both academically and personally. Our nurturing ethos ensures that our children and staff feel valued and supported to achieve their potential.
I am delighted to welcome you to our small but growing community primary school where dedicated staff, committed to delivering an inspirational and inclusive curriculum, provide a range of learning experiences which build on children’s interests and talents.
Badgemore Primary School . Henley-on-Thames . The Village School in the Heart of Town
Vision, Value and Ethos
Our overriding aim at Badgemore is to provide a nurturing ethos within which children and adults feel valued and supported to achieve their potential.

School Tours
Choosing the right school for you and your child.
When looking at different school and the options available to you it can seem overwhelming and a difficult decision; schools are mini communities, each with their own ethos, vision and culture and children are individuals, often suited to one school more than another.
It is important, therefore, to be able to make an informed choice about potential schools and to be able to ask questions and to see first-hand what different schools can offer your child.
For this reason Badgemore offers parents individual appointments with the Headteacher when visiting our school, including a tour of the school and grounds, giving you the opportunity to see the school on a normal working day and to meet staff and our children. You will have the chance to ask questions or request further information.
To arrange a tour, please contact the school office on telephone: 01491 575 665 or email: [email protected]

Music
At Badgemore, we aim to:
To provide a rich, diverse, and progressive music curriculum for all children (including during school hours and after school). This will be delivered through music teaching and leadership.
Provide opportunities to learn musical instruments, and participate in ensembles in school, along with regular performances, both in and out of school will showcase our children. This will also maximise cultural capital for all our children, their overall wellbeing and confidence, while creating a supportive community of music making.
Badgemore’s Music Development Plan sets out how we will deliver high-quality music provision in curriculum music, extra-curricular music and musical experiences, taking into account the key features in the national plan for music education.

SEND & Inclusion
Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
Badgemore Primary School is committed to providing an inclusive education that meets the needs of all our learners, including those children with additional learning needs.
Badgemore provides a very nurturing environment for vulnerable learners and we are fortunate to have teaching and support staff with a range of knowledge and skills to support our SEN pupils.
Badgemore SENCoGaynor Styer
Email: [email protected]Tel: 01491575665
SENDIASS
TeParent Partnership Oxfordshire has formed part of the new SEN and Disability Information, Advice and Support Service (SENDIASS) in Oxfordshire.
This new service has two arms, one offering impartial information, advice and support to parents of children and young people with SEN and disabilities, still called Parent Partnership, and the other providing the same service to the young people themselves.
Parent Partnership Oxfordshire aims to help parents, carers and educational professionals to work together to provide the best possible support to children with special educational needs, by:
We encourage everyone working with a child or young person to consider the child’s own views about their education.xt

An E-Group for parents of disabled children in Oxfordshire. The aim of this group is to form a strong parent / carer led group which aims to lead the consultation process to develop the services families need. In addition the e-group can be a place for information sharing, support and advice. Interested?… email Gail Hanrahan at [email protected]
SEN Talking Points
Want to find out about the SEN system? Looking for a chance to talk things through? Free drop-in sessions offering impartial information and advice at a centre near you. To find out more ring 01865 810516

The group is for parents / carers who have children diagnosed with or are in the process of being diagnosed with Aspergers, Autism, Dyspraxia and ADHD. The group meets in Didcot. For details contact Amanda Jones (Home School Link Worker) on 07825 823449 or Teresa Connelly (Parent) on 07787818872

Enrichment Clubs & Activities
Giving children more experiences
The school is lucky enough to be able to provide a number of extra-curricular activities both during the school day as well as after school.
Some of these activities are run by the school staff and others by external agencies such as Premier Sports. They are subject to change throughout the school year, providing an enriched experience for your child.
All Extra-Curricular After School Club Activities will start the second week of the full term and continue straight after half term breaks.

Music Lessons
Music lessons are provided through Henley Music School. Currently HMS provides Badgemore Primary School with both individual instrumental lessons, as well as full-class instrumental lessons.

HMS do also have bursaries of up to 100% available on all services, and pupil premium children automatically receive a free place.
HMS also offer free loan of an instrument.
If you’d like to have a taster lesson and sign up for lessons, please email the Henley Music School’s manager for further details.

pageCache.text:
Winners of the Rupert House Football Tournament
In a display of determination, teamwork, and sheer joy for the game, the Badgemore Primary School Year 2 football team clinched victory yesterday at the Rupert House Football Tournament, securing a memorable Cup Final win that had parents and teachers beaming with pride.
The final proved to be the ultimate test. Facing a strong and energetic Danesfield team, Badgemore held their nerve, working tirelessly to regain possession and push forward. Their breakthrough came with a well‑worked team move that ended in a decisive finish.
Coaches praised the children not only for their skill but for their sportsmanship throughout the afternoon. Spectators noted how the players encouraged one another, celebrated each small success, and never let setbacks shake their focus.
For the Year 2 team, the win marks a milestone they’ll remember for years. For the school, it’s a testament to the growing strength of its sports programme and the spirit of its young athletes.
Badgemore can proudly say their future football stars are already shining.
18 March 20265 April 2026

pageCache.pageTitle: Mental Health & Wellbeing – Badgemore Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mental Health & Wellbeing
Supporting our Pupils and their families
We are keen for children to get support for any mental health issues they may have in a non-judgemental manner whilst also understanding their power as an individual to develop a positive and growth mindset.
Whilst we will do all we can to support the children in our care, we recognise that much of the support needs to come from the home, with this in mind we thought we would share some information and strategies that you may find helpful in the home (see below).
We would urge parents and carers to seek support if children’s mental health escalates.
Where to access additional support
Contact your child’s GP
Parenting 1to1 support
Advice, guidance & signposting
Targeted holiday activities
Advice for children and parents on a variety of mental health issues
Supporting your child at home
As a parent, understanding the links between brain and behaviour can be enlightening. You may want to help your child understand how our brains work, why they deal with situations in certain ways and, crucially, how we can begin to modify our responses.
The 3 parts of the brain it can be useful to explore with children are:
Conquer the Amygdala Hijack
Here are some activities you could try at home to understand the brain.
Ages 3-6 Feeling Factory
Help young children identify what they are feeling and how to describe it.
Very often, behaviour difficulties (amygdala hijacks) are a result of a young child not having the words to describe what they are feeling and being overwhelmed.
Practice by acting out faces and guessing each other’s feelings so that children become more familiar with different expressions
Ages 7-9 Settle your glitter!
Take a small plastic jar/bottle with a screw-on lid and fill it almost to the top with water. Add glitter glue/glitter. Screw the lid on tight and shake! Or use a snow globe.
Talk with your child about how the jar is like your brain. Notice how hard it is to see clearly when the glitter is spinning. Compare it to when the amygdala is in charge and it’s hard to think clearly and make good decisions. When the glitter has settled, compare it to what it’s like when the amygdala is calm and you can access your prefrontal cortex and make good decisions.
Ages 10-11
Have your child get familiar with things they can do to counter negative emotions. Some ideas might be exercise, deep breathing, writing feelings down, spending time with friends or family.
Mindful Awareness
Mindful awareness through focused attention is a valuable skill for both children and caregivers to learn and master. Children and adults who learn that mindful breathing helps to calm them down, which in turn allows them to think more clearly and act in a reflective manner, will be better able to regulate their emotions, reduce stress, and make better decisions.
Here are some activities you could try for teaching about the breath.
Ages 3-6
Have your child lie down on the floor and have a bean bag/soft toy on their stomach. Instruct them to quietly watch the object rise and fall with their breath.
Blow bubbles together and watch them fall to the ground.
Use pinwheels to practice using your breath making them go fast or slow.
Ages 7-9
Use the ‘smell the flowers, blow out the candle’ image to help children develop the skill of focussing attention through breathing.
Use a focussing tool like a glitter wand or liquid timer to help your child practice mindful breathing.
Ages 10-11
Cotton ball activity Each person has a cotton ball. Practice 1) blowing it past an object Practice 2) blowing it to hit a target Practice 3) practicing a gentle breath to push the cotton ball from the middle of the palm of the hand to the fingertips without letting it fall.
Five finger or Hand Breathing – all ages
An activity that can be used at a time when children are feeling overwhelmed.
Some further activities to aid relaxation and tension release
